title: §5.1 'single trailing newline OPTIONAL' contradicts §5.2 'no trailing bytes'; both reference hosts silently widen to arbitrary Unicode trim, and they disagree on a UTF-8 BOM
claim: The spec gives the verifier permission to emit one trailing newline but obligates the host to reject 'no trailing bytes' and any 'leading/trailing prefix or suffix around the object'. A literal host rejects a conforming verifier's `{...}\n`; a lenient host accepts anything its language's trim() strips. The two reference hosts both call trim(), so they accept `\r\n`, multiple blank lines, tabs, and even U+00A0/U+3000 padding that no spec sentence permits — and they DIVERGE on the same bytes: JavaScript String.prototype.trim strips U+FEFF, so spec/reference-host.js accepts a BOM-prefixed allow verdict, while Rust str::trim (Unicode White_Space, which excludes U+FEFF) makes spec/reference-host-rs reject it as unparseable_stdout. The suite cannot detect this because no vector emits the verdict with a newline, CRLF, BOM, or non-ASCII whitespace: well-behaved-allow.js writes the bare object with no newline, and leading-garbage.js uses ASCII prose as its prefix.
evidence: spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §5.1 (line 417): "The verifier MUST write exactly one `JSON.stringify(verdict)` to the host-facing stdout, at the very end. A single trailing newline is OPTIONAL."

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §5.2 (line 449): "The host MUST parse the verifier's stdout as exactly one JSON object with no trailing bytes, and MUST reject (treat as deny, §7) any of: stdout that is empty, not valid JSON, or contains a leading/trailing prefix or suffix around the object"
spec/reference-host.js:211 `const s = str.trim();` and spec/reference-host-rs/src/lib.rs:330 `let s = s.trim();` — both hosts widen 'no trailing bytes' to language-defined whitespace trimming

Runnable divergence check: `node -e 'console.log(JSON.stringify("\uFEFF{\"verdict\":\"allow\"}\n".trim()))'` prints `{"verdict":"allow"}` (BOM stripped → JS host allows); Rust `"\u{FEFF}{...}".trim()` leaves the BOM in place → serde_json parse fails → Rust host denies

spec/fixtures/host-conformance/well-behaved-allow.js writes `JSON.stringify({ verdict: 'allow' })` with no trailing newline — the OPTIONAL newline path that §5.1 explicitly permits is never exercised by any positive control
proposed_artifact: A staged §5.2 diff defining the exact tolerated framing (at most one trailing LF or CRLF, no leading bytes, no BOM, no other Unicode whitespace) plus three vectors: host-allow-trailing-newline (positive control), host-deny-bom-prefixed-allow, and host-deny-unicode-whitespace-padded-allow, with reference-host.js and reference-host-rs patched to byte-level framing instead of trim().

title: 'integer' is undefined at the JSON level: JSON Schema 2020-12 accepts 4102444800.0 and 1e10 as integers, the JS reference host agrees, the Rust reference host rejects them — same verdict bytes, opposite decisions
claim: The spec types `now_unix`, `version`, and `retain_until` as `integer` and points to a JSON Schema where `"type": "integer"` under draft 2020-12 matches ANY number with a zero fractional part, so `4102444800.0`, `4.1024448e9`, and `1e10` are all schema-valid integers. A hostile verifier that emits `"retain_until": 4102444800.0` is accepted by spec/reference-host.js (Number.isInteger(4102444800.0) === true) and rejected as schema_invalid by spec/reference-host-rs (requires serde is_i64()||is_u64(), and its own test asserts 1.5 is rejected but never tests 1.0 or 1e10). The same ambiguity applies on the request side: a host emitting `"now_unix": 1751990400.0` or `"version": 1.0` gets `malformed_input` from a Go/Rust verifier using int64 and `allow` from a JS or schema-validating verifier; nothing in §2.1 says which is conforming. Range is also unspecified: a JS host stores retain_until as a double, so `9007199254740993` silently rounds and two hosts durably record different retention deadlines for the same nonce. The conformance suite has no vector with a fractional-form, exponent-form, or >2^53 integer.
evidence: spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §2.1: "`now_unix` (integer, REQUIRED, positive) — the host's current wall-clock time in seconds since the Unix epoch." and "A request that is not a JSON object, is missing a REQUIRED field, or has a field of the wrong type MUST yield `deny code=malformed_input`"

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §2.2/§3.4 schema lines 119, 142, 239: `"version": { "type": "integer", "const": 1 }`, `"now_unix": { "type": "integer", "exclusiveMinimum": 0 }`, `"retain_until": { "type": "integer" }` with `"$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"` — JSON Schema Validation 2020-12 §6.1.1 defines integer as any number with a zero fractional part, so 1.0 and 1e10 validate

spec/reference-host.js:149 `if (!Number.isInteger(e.retain_until)) return false;` — accepts 4102444800.0 and 1e10; runnable: `node -e 'console.log(Number.isInteger(4102444800.0), Number.isInteger(1e10))'` prints `true true`

spec/reference-host-rs/src/lib.rs:430 `.is_some_and(|r| r.is_i64() || r.is_u64())` and lib.rs:734 test `e["retain_until"] = json!(1.5); // fraction` — serde_json parses `4102444800.0` and `1e10` as f64, so is_i64/is_u64 are false and the Rust host fails closed on a verdict the JS host accepts
Vector index (set 0.6.0): host-deny-nonce-entry-wrong-type covers a STRING retain_until only; no vector covers fractional-form, exponent-form, negative, or >2^53 integers
proposed_artifact: A staged diff adding a normative 'integer' definition to §2.1/§3.3 (RFC 8259 number with no fraction/exponent characters, range 0 < n < 2^53, verifier and host MUST reject others) plus vectors host-deny-retain-until-fractional-form, host-deny-retain-until-exponent-form, host-deny-retain-until-over-2p53, and a verifier-side malformed_input vector for `now_unix: 1751990400.0`, with the Rust and JS hosts aligned.

title: §7.2 'kill the process' does not say process tree: a verifier whose worker (the spec's OWN reference architecture) outlives the direct child holds the stdout pipe open, and the JS reference host hangs forever after its timeout kill
claim: §5.1 tells verifiers to spawn a worker process; §7.2 tells hosts to 'kill the process' on timeout. Nothing says the host must kill descendants. A lazy verifier that spawns its worker detached (or simply is killed before it can reap the worker) leaves a grandchild holding an inherited fd 1. spec/reference-host.js calls child.kill('SIGKILL') on the direct child only and then waits for the 'close' event, which Node fires only after every stdio stream reaches EOF — so with a grandchild holding stdout open, the host has already 'timed out' but never emits a decision: the timeout is not a deadline, it is a hang. spec/reference-host-rs explicitly diverges: it puts the verifier in its own process group and kill_process_group()s it with a 100 ms drain grace, citing §16.3 'nothing outlives the decision' — a rule that appears only in a Rust comment, not in normative text. Every kill-proof fixture (no-output-hang, partial-json-hang, slow-allow-past-deadline, oversize-flood) is single-process and records only its own PID, so the suite cannot distinguish the two reference hosts, and the runner's orphan check would miss a grandchild anyway because _pidfile.js records one PID.
evidence: spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §7.2 (line 497): "timeout (§6) — the host MUST kill the process and deny;" — singular 'the process', no mention of descendants or process group

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §5.1: "the command spawns a worker process that performs the entire verification; the worker's stdio binds fd 0 = request in, fd 1 = captured ... fd 2 = inherited parent stderr" — the reference verifier architecture is multi-process by mandate

spec/reference-host.js:70 `const timer = setTimeout(() => { timedOut = true; child.kill('SIGKILL'); }, timeoutMs);` kills only the direct child; the decision is emitted only inside `child.on('close', ...)` (line 85), and Node's 'close' fires only after all stdio streams close

spec/reference-host-rs/src/lib.rs:182-185 comment + `command.process_group(0);` and lib.rs:269-281 "If something still holds the pipe open past the budget, kill the whole process group: nothing outlives the decision (§16.3)." — the Rust host implements a stronger obligation than the spec states, i.e. the two reference hosts diverge on the same fixture class
spec/fixtures/host-conformance/_pidfile.js records `String(process.pid)` only; no fixture in spec/fixtures/host-conformance/ spawns a child process, so no vector exercises a grandchild holding fd 1

Runnable reproduction: fixture `require('child_process').spawn(process.execPath, ['-e','setInterval(()=>{},1<<30)'], {stdio:['ignore','inherit','inherit'], detached:true}); setInterval(()=>{},1<<30)` fed to `HOST_CMD='node spec/reference-host.js'` with HUT_TIMEOUT_MS=2000 never returns a decision
proposed_artifact: A new vector host-deny-orphaned-worker-holds-stdout (verifier spawns a detached grandchild inheriting fd 1 and hangs; expected deny/timeout within HUT_TIMEOUT_MS plus grace, and runner asserts the grandchild PID is dead) plus a staged §6/§7.2 diff making 'kill' mean the whole process tree / group and making the deadline hard even when the pipe stays open, with a reference-host.js fix (detached spawn + process-group kill + decide-on-timer instead of on 'close').

title: §2 obligates the host to write the whole request then close stdin, but never says what happens when the verifier does not read it; the §10/draft pseudocode deadlocks on any request larger than the OS pipe buffer
claim: The host-side pseudocode the spec and the I-D both present is `write(child.stdin, json(request)); close(child.stdin)` followed by `wait(child)` with the timeout as a spawn parameter. A verifier that never reads stdin (or stops reading at its §6 bound and keeps running) leaves a synchronous host blocked in write() once the request exceeds the pipe buffer (64 KiB on Linux, 16–64 KiB on macOS) — and a host that arms its timer after the write, as the pseudocode's ordering invites, never reaches the timeout at all. A verifier that closes stdin early instead produces EPIPE/SIGPIPE, which the spec never mentions; a naive host is killed by SIGPIPE (default disposition) with no decision, a fail-open-by-crash for any caller that treats 'no decision' as 'not denied'. Both reference hosts quietly handle this (JS: `child.stdin.on('error', () => {})`, Rust: a dedicated writer thread swallowing write errors), so the obligation exists in code but not in normative text. Every hang fixture drains stdin (`process.stdin.resume()`), and the runner's canned request is ~200 bytes, so the suite never sends a request large enough to fill a pipe and never spawns a verifier that refuses to read — a host that deadlocks here passes 28/28.
evidence: spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §2: "The host MUST write exactly one JSON object, UTF-8 encoded, to the verifier's stdin and then MUST close (EOF) stdin." — an unconditional MUST with no failure branch for a verifier that does not consume stdin

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §6: "The verifier MUST bound the request read from stdin. The reference limit is 1 MiB (1 048 576 bytes). A request over the bound MUST yield `deny code=malformed_input`; the verifier MUST NOT buffer an unbounded request." — a verifier is thus permitted to stop reading mid-request, which is exactly the condition that blocks a synchronous writer

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §10 (line 622) and spec/draft-kondoju-evc-01.md §3 pseudocode: `write(child.stdin, json(request)); close(child.stdin)` then `status, out, err = wait(child)` — the normative-looking host recipe writes synchronously before waiting

spec/reference-host.js:96-99 comment "Swallow EPIPE from a verifier that never reads stdin." and spec/reference-host-rs/src/lib.rs:193-203 "Errors (e.g. EPIPE from a verifier that dies without reading stdin) are deliberately" ignored via a writer thread — both hosts implement an unstated obligation

spec/fixtures/host-conformance/no-output-hang.js `process.stdin.resume();` (drains stdin) and spec/conformance-runner.js:42 canned request `bundle: 'host-conformance-placeholder-bundle'` (tiny) — no vector combines a non-reading verifier with a request larger than a pipe buffer

Runnable reproduction: fixture `setInterval(()=>{},1<<30)` (no stdin read) with a vector request whose bundle is a 512 KiB string, run against a host that does `child.stdin.write(req); await wait` synchronously — blocks indefinitely; the same fixture against `node spec/reference-host.js` returns timeout
proposed_artifact: A new vector host-deny-verifier-never-reads-stdin-large-request (verifier ignores stdin and hangs; request carries a ~512 KiB in-bound bundle; expected deny with failure_class timeout within HUT_TIMEOUT_MS) plus a staged §2/§6 diff stating the host MUST write stdin asynchronously or under the same wall-clock deadline, MUST treat EPIPE/SIGPIPE on the stdin write as a non-fatal condition that still ends in a decision, and MUST arm the timeout at spawn time, with a §10 pseudocode correction.

title: Host nonce mode silently accepts a bare `allow` with no `consume_nonces` — replay protection vanishes with no signal
claim: In host nonce mode the verifier does NOT persist nonces (§8) and the host only reserves when `consume_nonces` is present. A verifier that ignores/does not implement `--nonce-mode host` (a misconfigured local-mode spawn, or an `external`-class verifier without nonce support) returns a bare `{"verdict":"allow"}`; both reference hosts then call recordAction() and authorize with NOBODY recording the nullifier, so the same bundle replays indefinitely until expiry. §3.2 legitimizes the omission ('the key is omitted entirely when there is nothing to burn') while §9 already defines `nonce_missing` as a deny for 'the proof lacks a usable nullifier' — the two are contradictory in host mode: a presentation with nothing to burn should have been `deny code=nonce_missing`, so a bare allow reaching a host-mode host is a protocol violation the host must fail closed on. No vector exercises HUT_NONCE_MODE=host with a bare allow.
evidence: spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §3.2 (pinned a4f546f): 'consume_nonces (array of objects, OPTIONAL, allow-only). When present it is a non-empty list (the key is omitted entirely when there is nothing to burn).'

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §8: 'host. The verifier does not persist nonces. On an otherwise-allow it returns consume_nonces … and the host owns durable storage under the reserve-before-act rule (§7.3).'
spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §9: 'nonce_missing | the proof lacks a usable nullifier / session-nonce signal.'

spec/reference-host.js:117-124 — `if (nonceMode === 'host' && Array.isArray(v.consume_nonces)) { if (!reserveAll(...)) return deny replay } recordAction(); return finish({decision:'allow'})` — a bare allow in host mode skips reservation and authorizes.
spec/reference-host-rs/src/lib.rs:542-550 — identical shape: `if cfg.host_nonce_mode { if let Some(entries) = verdict.get("consume_nonces") … }` then `record_action`; `Decision::Allow`.

Runnable: `HUT_NONCE_MODE=host HUT_NONCE_STORE=/tmp/ns HUT_ACTION_LOG=/tmp/al HUT_VERIFIER_CMD='["node","spec/fixtures/host-conformance/well-behaved-allow.js"]' HUT_TIMEOUT_MS=5000 HUT_MAX_STDOUT_BYTES=65536 node spec/reference-host.js < <(node -e 'process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({version:1,bundle:"x",request:{agent_name:"a",project_key:"p",program:"c",model:"m",granted_capabilities:[]},now_unix:1751990400}))')` → `{"decision":"allow"}` with an empty nonce store and an action marker written.
Vector index 0.6.0: all three `host-nonce-*` vectors drive `allow-consume-nonces*.js`; no host_behavior vector pairs HUT_NONCE_MODE=host with `well-behaved-allow.js`.
proposed_artifact: Staged spec diff adding to §7.3/§8 a normative rule that in host nonce mode an `allow` without `consume_nonces` MUST be treated by the host as fail-closed (new §16.3 class `nonce_unconsumed`), plus a new host_behavior vector `host-deny-host-mode-bare-allow` (HUT_NONCE_MODE=host + well-behaved-allow.js → deny, action_taken:false) and the two-line fix to both reference hosts.

title: `retain_until` is unconstrained: no MUST ties it to effective expiry and a past/zero value lets a production host evict the nonce while the credential is still valid
claim: §7.3 obligates the host to retain a reserved nonce 'until entry.retain_until', but the verdict schema types it as a bare `integer` (no minimum) and the spec never states the invariant the reference verifier actually implements (retain_until == effectiveExpiry). A production host with expiry-based eviction (which §16.2 explicitly anticipates: 'expiry columns') that receives `retain_until: 0`, a negative value, or any value below the credential's effective expiry will garbage-collect the reservation and accept a replay of the same bundle before `now_unix >= expiry` fires. The harness cannot see this because both reference stores ignore retain_until entirely. The spec should (a) require the verifier to set retain_until >= the effective expiry it evaluated, (b) require the host to fail closed on retain_until <= now_unix (a zero-length reservation is meaningless), and (c) tighten the schema to `minimum: 1`.
evidence: spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §3.4 verdict schema (pinned a4f546f): `"retain_until": { "type": "integer" }` — no minimum, no relation to expiry.

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §7.3 step 1: 'atomically insert entry.nonce into durable storage with a unique-insert / "on conflict reject" semantic, retaining it until entry.retain_until.' — the only normative use of the field.

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §16.2: 'A production host with a different store (SQLite, a KV, issuer-scoped keys, expiry columns) tests against this suite by pointing a thin test adapter at this file format' — expiry-based eviction is an anticipated production shape.

integrations/cli/src/verify/core.ts:331 — `const retainUntil = Number(effectiveExpiry);` — the reference verifier's invariant (retain_until equals effective expiry) is implemented but nowhere stated normatively.

spec/reference-host.js:181-202 reserveAll() and spec/reference-host-rs/src/lib.rs reserve_all(): store only `e.nonce`; retain_until is read for type-checking only and never persisted, so the suite is blind to eviction behaviour.
spec/reference-host-rs/src/lib.rs:392 doc comment: '`retain_until` must parse as a JSON integer (i64/u64)' — negative values are accepted as valid.
Existing vector `host-deny-nonce-entry-wrong-type` covers only a string-typed retain_until; no vector covers retain_until <= now_unix or retain_until < expiry.
proposed_artifact: Staged spec diff (§3.2/§3.4/§7.3/§8) adding `minimum: 1` to retain_until, a verifier MUST that retain_until >= effective_expiry, and a host MUST fail-closed (`schema_invalid`) when retain_until <= request.now_unix, plus new fixture `nonce-entry-retain-until-past.js` and vector `host-deny-nonce-retain-until-past` and updates to both reference hosts' validators.

title: No vector proves the host's timeout covers the stdin WRITE phase — a verifier that never reads stdin plus a request larger than the pipe buffer wedges a naive host forever
claim: §6 says the host must enforce a wall-clock timeout 'on the spawned process', and every hang fixture drains stdin first (`process.stdin.resume()`), so a host that writes the request synchronously and only then arms/awaits its timeout passes the whole suite. Against a verifier that blocks before reading stdin (crash-looping loader, stuck WASM init, or a hostile external verifier) and a request larger than the OS pipe buffer (64 KiB on Linux/macOS; the contract permits requests up to 1 MiB and the bundle is attacker-influenced), such a host blocks in write() indefinitely — a fail-closed-by-hang that never produces a decision and, in a thread-per-request host, is a denial-of-service lever. Both reference hosts happen to be safe (async end() / detached writer thread) but that is unproven by the suite, and the Python idiom `p.stdin.write(req); p.stdin.close(); p.wait(timeout)` is the obvious way a third-party host gets it wrong.
evidence: spec/fixtures/host-conformance/no-output-hang.js (pinned a4f546f): 'verifier reads stdin, writes NOTHING, and never exits' — `process.stdin.resume();` drains the pipe so the host's write always completes.

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §6: 'The host MUST enforce a wall-clock timeout on the spawned process and treat expiry as deny (§7). The RECOMMENDED timeout is 10 000 ms' — silent on whether the request-write phase is inside the budget.
spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §6: 'The reference limit is 1 MiB (1 048 576 bytes)' — legitimate requests can exceed the 64 KiB pipe capacity by 16x.

spec/reference-host.js:96-99 — comment 'Swallow EPIPE from a verifier that never reads stdin' + non-blocking `child.stdin.end(request)` after the timer at line 70; spec/reference-host-rs/src/lib.rs:193-204 — 'The handle is dropped (detached): the host never blocks on the writer'. Both hosts reason about this hazard in comments, yet no vector asserts it.

Runnable reproduction of the hazard in a third-party host shape: `python3 -c "import subprocess,json,sys; p=subprocess.Popen(['node','-e','setInterval(()=>{},1e9)'],stdin=subprocess.PIPE,stdout=subprocess.PIPE); req=json.dumps({'version':1,'bundle':'A'*200000,'request':{'agent_name':'a','project_key':'p','program':'c','model':'m','granted_capabilities':[]},'now_unix':1}).encode(); p.stdin.write(req); p.stdin.close(); print(p.wait(timeout=5))"` — blocks in write() forever and never reaches the timeout.
§16.1 lists four 'kill-proof' fixtures; none combines an unread stdin with a request > 64 KiB.
proposed_artifact: New host_behavior vector `host-deny-stdin-unread-hang` with fixture `stdin-unread-hang.js` (records PID, never reads fd 0, never exits) and a runner-supplied request padded past 256 KiB, asserting `failure_class: timeout` within HUT_TIMEOUT_MS + slack and a killed pidfile PID, plus a one-sentence §6 clarification that the timeout budget MUST include the request write.

title: Binding v2 rules (five-field v1 → unsupported_version, binding.expiry ≠ credential.expiry → invalid_bundle, now_unix == expiry → expired) have no external_verifier IO-contract vectors
claim: §4.1 introduces three MUSTs that exist only because of the classical/external re-anchoring attack (a presenter re-signing a later expiry onto an issued mandate), yet the `external_verifier` class in vector set 0.6.0 contains ten vectors and none of them presents a bundle at the stdin/stdout boundary that (a) carries an obsolete five-field binding, (b) carries a binding.expiry that differs from the credential expiry, or (c) sets now_unix exactly equal to the effective expiry. The equality boundary is covered only in the `handshake` and `delegation` classes (SDK-level, not the EVC boundary), and the binding-v1 / expiry-mismatch cases are covered nowhere. An independent verifier vendor (e.g. the mcp-use-evc-example implementer, or any `classical`-kind verifier) can pass the published `@bolyra/evc-conformance` suite while accepting a re-anchored expiry — exactly the gap v2 was shipped to close. Spec-hardness coverage (% of normative MUSTs backed by a vector) is measurably lower for §4.1 than for any other section.
evidence: spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §4.1 (pinned a4f546f): 'A verifier MUST reject a binding that omits expiry with deny code=unsupported_version — it is an obsolete binding v1 (five fields, expiry not signature-bound) and, in a classical- or external-class verifier where the proof does not independently bind expiry, would let a presenter re-anchor a later expiry on an issued mandate.'

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §4.1: 'After the binding signature verifies, a verifier MUST additionally require binding.expiry == credential.expiry … rejecting a mismatch deny code=invalid_bundle'.
spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §9: 'expired | proof-anchored now_unix >= effective_expiry — a strict comparison; the equality boundary is rejected.'

spec/test-vectors.json (set 0.6.0) `external_verifier` ids: external-verifier-allow-agent, external-verifier-allow-host-nonce, external-verifier-deny-malformed-input, external-verifier-deny-scope-exceeded, external-verifier-deny-model-mismatch, external-verifier-kind-zk-default, external-verifier-kind-zk-explicit, external-verifier-kind-classical-allow, external-verifier-kind-external-deny, external-verifier-kind-invalid-rejected — no expiry, binding-v1, or expiry-mismatch case.
Equality boundary exists only outside the EVC boundary: `expired-credential-exact-boundary` (handshake class) and `delegation-expiry-equal` (delegation class) in spec/test-vectors.json.

integrations/cli/src/verify/core.ts:249-256 implements the binding.expiry == cred.expiry check and :312-313 the strict expiry check — implemented in the reference verifier but not pinned by any IO-contract vector a third-party verifier must pass.

Runnable coverage check: `node -e 'const v=require("./spec/test-vectors.json");console.log((v.vectors||v).filter(x=>x.type==="external_verifier"&&/expir|binding/.test(x.id+x.description)).length)'` → 0.
proposed_artifact: Three new `external_verifier` vectors with pinned golden bundles — `external-verifier-deny-binding-v1-five-field` (unsupported_version), `external-verifier-deny-binding-expiry-mismatch` (invalid_bundle), `external-verifier-deny-expiry-equal-boundary` (expired, now_unix == expiry) — plus the golden regeneration and `node integrations/evc-conformance/scripts/sync.js` steps in APPLY.md.

title: EVC request envelope authorizes a capability class, never the concrete action; verifiable-intent/AP2 bind the transaction itself
claim: Mastercard's verifiable-intent (layered SD-JWT chain) and AP2's Intent/Cart Mandates bind authorization to the specific transaction (payee, amount, cart digest), while the EVC v1 request carries only agent_name/project_key/program/model/granted_capabilities. A host that gets `allow` for capability `send_payment` has no contract-level way to bind that verdict to THIS payment, so two distinct actions of the same capability class are indistinguishable at the wire boundary. @bolyra/mpp already computes a bare-64-hex `commerce.intentHash` (integrations/mpp-payments/src/receipts.ts:224) and the receipt format carries it, but the EVC request schema has no slot for it — the intent binding lives above the contract, so an `external`-class verifier cannot be handed the action digest and cannot bind to it. Because the request schema is `additionalProperties: true`, an OPTIONAL `request.intent_hash` (64 lowercase hex, SHA-256 of a host-canonicalized action) can be added within wire major 1 with a rule that a verifier that does not understand it MUST ignore it (host-side binding), and a verifier that does understand it MUST compare literally against the bundle's binding when the binding carries one.
evidence: spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §2.1: 'request (object, REQUIRED) — the privileged action the host is about to authorize. It MUST contain: agent_name … project_key … program … model … granted_capabilities' — no action payload / intent digest field
spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §2.2 request schema: '"additionalProperties": true' on both the top-level and `request` objects — an OPTIONAL field is additive within major 1

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §9 request_mismatch row: 'a host request field does not match the signed binding, or granted_capabilities are not covered by the binding's capabilities' — mismatch is defined only over the five context fields
integrations/mpp-payments/src/receipts.ts:222-224: commerce.intentHash = sha256Hex(...) enforced against /^[0-9a-fA-F]{64}$/ — the intent digest exists in the product but not in the contract

https://github.com/agent-intent/verifiable-intent/ — 'Layered SD-JWT credential format creating a tamper-evident chain that proves an AI agent's actions stayed within the scope delegated by a human user' (Mastercard-maintained)
https://arxiv.org/html/2608.23858v1 — AP2 Intent and Cart Mandates: 'how mandates prove buyer authorization for agent transactions'

title: AuthZEN AARP and AIP define a third 'hold / prerequisite-pending' outcome; EVC's binary allow|deny has no documented mapping for it
claim: The OpenID AuthZEN Access Request and Approval Profile (AARP) exists precisely for the case where 'policy cannot yet authorize an action because a prerequisite (approval, consent, delegated authority, attestation, risk assessment) must first be satisfied', and draft-aip-agent-identity-protocol-00 produces 'allow/deny/hold decisions'. EVC v1 has exactly two verdict values and a closed 15-code deny registry, none of which means 'not yet — a step-up is required'. A host wiring EVC behind an AuthZEN PDP or an AIP proxy must invent a mapping, and the only safe one (hold ⇒ deny) discards the prerequisite information. This is defensible fail-closed design, but it is undocumented: the spec should state normatively that a verifier MUST NOT emit any third verdict value, that a pending-prerequisite condition is expressed as `deny` with an existing code (the natural choice is `scope_exceeded` or `request_mismatch`) and the prerequisite carried in `detail` (e.g. `detail.prerequisite`), and that hosts implementing an approval loop re-invoke the verifier with a new bundle rather than caching a 'hold'. Without this, the competing framing ('EVC can't express approval workflows') stands unanswered.
evidence: spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §3: 'The verdict is one of three shapes' (allow / allow+consume_nonces / deny) and §3.3: 'verdict (string, REQUIRED) — "allow" or "deny"'

title: Agent Receipts / AERF / AAR make the decision record part of the protocol; EVC's verdict has no correlation handle a receipt can cite
claim: The agent-receipts protocol, the Agent Evidence Receipt Format referenced in agno#6892, and the tracked agent-action-receipt-spec all treat 'what was decided, by whom, on which input' as a first-class durable record. EVC deliberately excludes durability, and @bolyra/receipts covers it in-product (ReceiptPayload.decision, proof.*Hash fields), but the two are not joined at the contract: the verdict envelope carries no verifier-emitted identifier, no digest of the request it decided, and no verifier identity, so a receipt written by the host cannot cite the specific verifier run except by the host's own bookkeeping. A competitor can truthfully say 'EVC verdicts are unattributable'. Because the allow/deny schemas are `additionalProperties: false`, this cannot be fixed within wire major 1 by adding a field; the honest -02 answer is (a) an informative 'Durable records' section that specifies how a host binds a receipt to a run (host records sha256 of the exact stdin bytes + verifier argv + verdict bytes) and (b) a registered -02/major-2 candidate `decision_ref` field. The section must say explicitly that receipts are host-owned and the contract stays transport-only, which is the moat-safe framing.
evidence: spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §3.4: both the allow and deny schemas declare '"additionalProperties": false' — no room for a verifier-emitted decision id within major 1

spec/draft-kondoju-evc-01.md §1.3 'What EVC Deliberately Excludes': 'EVC does not define credential issuance, the internal proof format, policy authoring, delegation semantics, revocation infrastructure, or any PKI' — durable decision records are neither excluded nor addressed

title: draft-klrc/DAAP/OBO delegation is auditable token-by-token; EVC's `delegation_invalid` collapses four failure classes into one code — prove the `detail` echo already disambiguates
claim: draft-klrc-aiagent-auth-03 and draft-mishra-oauth-agent-grants-01 (DAAP) build delegation on OAuth token exchange, where every hop is a separately inspectable token and a failing hop yields a distinct, locatable error. EVC folds 'chain break, hop-cap overflow (> 3 hops), scope expansion, or expiry expansion' into the single wire code `delegation_invalid`, and the hop cap (3) appears only in a table cell, not as a normative MUST. A competing-spec author argues EVC delegation failures are undebuggable across a host boundary. The rebuttal already exists in the spec text — §3.3 says a verifier SHOULD echo the originating internal code in `detail` (e.g. `sdk_code`) — but no public artifact demonstrates that the reference verifier actually emits a distinguishing `detail` for each of the four sub-causes. This is an evidence gap, not a spec gap: a pinned, reproducible run record showing four `delegation_invalid` verdicts with four distinct `detail.sdk_code` values (and one showing the > 3 hop overflow) neutralizes the argument and doubles as RFC 7942 implementation-experience material for -02.

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §8: 'Delegation hops add no entry: each per-hop delegation nullifier is bound to the agent's session nonce' — delegation replay coverage is asserted, not demonstrated by any published vector

title: Draft §6.3 never defines the stdout output bound that §9 Security Considerations and the oversize_stdout failure class depend on
claim: The draft's Timeout and Input Bounds section specifies only the stdin bound (1 MiB) and the timeout (10 s). The Security Considerations section then says 'The stdout output bound and the stdin bound (Section 6.3) bound a hostile verifier ... the host MUST enforce both', and the failure-class table defines oversize_stdout as 'stdout exceeded the host output bound' — but no section states what that bound is, whether it is host-chosen, or a RECOMMENDED value. A host implementer reading the draft alone cannot know whether a 4 KiB or 100 MiB bound is conformant; the only numeric value lives outside the draft (reference hosts default to 1048576 via HUT_MAX_STDOUT_BYTES). A MUST that references an undefined quantity is an IESG DISCUSS-class gap.
evidence: draft-kondoju-evc-01 §6.3 (Timeout and Input Bounds), full text: 'The verifier MUST bound the request read from stdin; the reference limit is 1 MiB (1 048 576 bytes)...' — no stdout bound appears.

spec/external-verifier-contract-v1.md §16.2: 'HUT_MAX_STDOUT_BYTES — the stdout output bound the host MUST enforce (§6)' — §6 of the v1 spec likewise contains no stdout bound value.
proposed_artifact: Staged diff to draft-kondoju-evc-01 §6.3 (and v1 spec §6) adding: 'The host MUST bound the bytes it accepts from the verifier's stdout and MUST kill the process and deny on breach; the RECOMMENDED bound is 1 MiB (1 048 576 bytes), matching the reference hosts. A conforming verdict is never larger than a few kilobytes.' plus a cross-reference from §9 and the failure-class table, and an APPLY.md noting no wire change and no golden regeneration.

title: RFC 7942 Implementation Status lists the only independent host at vector set 0.5.0 (27/27) while the draft claims a 28-vector 0.6.0 suite, and omits the RFC 7942 licensing/contact/coverage fields

title: Non-BCP-14 capitalized keyword FORBIDDEN (twice) and normative MUSTs imposed on consumers of an unreferenced sibling document (RSD)
claim: Two RFC 2119/8174 hygiene defects an idnits/area review will flag. (a) The draft uses 'FORBIDDEN' in all capitals as if it were a requirement keyword in §7.2 and again in §9 ('"Record after proceeding" is a replay window and is FORBIDDEN'). FORBIDDEN is not in the BCP 14 list the draft itself enumerates in §2, so the sentence carries no defined normative force — the single most important replay obligation is stated with an undefined keyword. (b) §10 (Relationship to Receipt Signer Discovery) and §9 (Redirect and Downgrade in Signer Discovery) place four MUSTs on 'a consumer' of a document called RSD ('a consumer MUST fetch over HTTPS ... MUST NOT follow redirects ... MUST treat any transport, status, or schema failure as a verification failure ... MUST require the two to agree'), yet RSD appears in neither the normative nor the informative reference list, has no URL, and §12.3 says its Internet-Draft is 'deferred past this document'. A reviewer cannot resolve what a 'consumer' is or verify the imported rules; per RFC 2119 §6 keywords are for interoperation requirements of this specification, and imported requirements on an unreferenced spec are unimplementable-as-written. The same section also contains a lowercase 'must' at §5.3/§13 that reads as normative ('a "zk"-class verifier that must remain interoperable').
evidence: draft-kondoju-evc-01 line 625 (§7.2): '"Record after proceeding" is a replay window and is FORBIDDEN. The verifier's "allow" in host mode is conditional on every host insert being novel.'
draft-kondoju-evc-01 line 978 (§9 Nonce Reservation and Replay): 'proceeding" is a replay window and is FORBIDDEN.'

draft-kondoju-evc-01 §2 keyword list: 'The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" ...' — FORBIDDEN absent.

draft-kondoju-evc-01 front matter lines 24-36: normative refs are RFC2119, RFC8174, RFC8259; informative refs are RFC6749, RFC7519, RFC7662, RFC7942, RFC8126, RFC8615, I-D.klrc-aiagent-auth, I-D.pidlisnyi-aps — no RSD entry.

draft-kondoju-evc-01 §10: 'A sibling specification, Receipt Signer Discovery (RSD), defines a ".well-known/bolyra-signers.json" document ... a consumer MUST fetch over HTTPS, and plain "http://" MUST be rejected except for loopback addresses (development); a consumer MUST NOT follow redirects; and a consumer MUST treat any transport or schema failure as a verification failure'
draft-kondoju-evc-01 §12.3: 'A separate RSD Internet-Draft ... is deferred past this document'
proposed_artifact: Staged diff to draft-kondoju-evc-01: replace both FORBIDDEN sentences with 'A host MUST NOT record a nonce after proceeding with the action; doing so opens a replay window', rewrite the RSD rules in §9/§10 as either (i) conditional requirements scoped to this document ('A classical-class verifier that consumes a signer-discovery document MUST ...') or (ii) an informative paraphrase with a new informative reference [RSD] carrying a URL to the RSD spec text in the repo, and lowercase-fix the two 'must remain interoperable' sentences; APPLY.md notes prose-only, no wire change.

title: -02 blocker: draft body cites repository-relative file paths (spec/reference-host.js, spec/test-vectors.json) instead of reference entries with URLs
claim: Seven places in the draft identify artifacts by repo-relative path strings such as "spec/reference-host.js", "spec/reference-host-rs/", "spec/test-vectors.json", and the fixture filename "allow-consume-nonces.js". These paths are meaningful only inside the bolyra/bolyra checkout; the RFC Editor and any reviewer reading the datatracker rendering have no way to resolve them, and they are not stable across renames. RFC 7942 and normal I-D practice expect implementations and test material to be cited via reference entries with a URL (and, for reproducibility, a pinned commit or published package version). The published @bolyra/evc-conformance@0.2.0 package already provides a stable citation target for the suite, and the two reference hosts can be cited by GitHub URL plus the a4f546f commit. Additionally, the host-side pseudocode in §3 checks 'status != 0' before 'timed_out' — the reverse of the SHOULD precedence in §6.4 ('the host's own kills first (output bound, then timeout), then ... a non-zero exit') — and should either follow that order or be labeled as illustrative-only so the two do not read as contradictory.

draft-kondoju-evc-01 lines 648-649: '28 "host_behavior" vectors, confirmed in "spec/test-vectors.json": the "allow-consume-nonces.js" fixture drives two vectors'

title: OpenID AuthZEN WG drafts (COAZ, AARP) define a competing decision envelope for MCP tool authorization with a third 'prerequisite pending' outcome
claim: The OpenID Foundation AuthZEN Working Group approved two WG drafts: the AuthZEN Profile for Model Context Protocol Tool Authorization (COAZ) and the Access Request and Approval Profile (AARP). AuthZEN is an HTTP PEP↔PDP evaluation API (subject/action/resource/context → decision), so COAZ places a standards-body decision envelope at precisely the point EVC occupies — the gate in front of an MCP tool call — with existing vendor interop behind it. AARP additionally models the case where policy cannot yet authorize because approval, consent, delegated authority, attestation, or risk assessment must first be satisfied; EVC's verdict is strictly allow/deny with a closed 15-code registry and no pending state. Counter available: EVC is proof-system-agnostic and offline; a PDP can spawn an EVC verifier (kind=classical|zk|external) as the evidence check that produces the AuthZEN decision, and denial codes map into AuthZEN response context. Falsification: read the COAZ draft text; if it already specifies a pluggable local verifier or an offline proof-bundle check, the overlap is larger than modeled and the card's counter_available dimension drops.

title: No host_behavior vector exercises §5.3 'Hosts MUST NOT parse stderr for the verdict'
claim: None of the 27 fixtures writes anything to stderr; every vector proves fail-closed on stdout shapes only.
